answer: Each agent must hold a cedar token whose secure enclave maintains a hash-chained monotonic counter; a bonded registrar verifies each ticket against the token serial. A public ledge accepts only one non-transferable ticket per serial per epoch and rejects any fork, so extra identities require extra tokens at cost C amortized over L epochs plus renewal f; n identities gain n(R - C/L - f) and profit only while R > C/L + f. The fable that one token can sign for many keys is false; enclave compromise or token resale remains the weakness.
